title: Tools Need Not Speak in Text: Latent Context Compression for Agents
title_zh: 工具无需以文本说话：面向智能体的潜在上下文压缩

paragraphs.en: Large language model (LLM) agents typically append raw tool outputs to their context. Over multi-step interactions, long and noisy observations incur substantial context overhead and dilute the agent’s attention to task-relevant information. Existing token pruning and summarization methods remain constrained by discrete text representations, limiting the achievable compression ratios.
paragraphs.zh: 大语言模型（LLM）智能体通常将原始工具输出直接附加到其上下文中。 在多步交互过程中，冗长且嘈杂的观测结果会带来大量的上下文开销，并稀释智能体对任务相关信息的注意力。 现有的 token 剪枝与摘要方法仍受限于离散文本表示，限制了可实现的压缩比率。

sents.en: Large language model (LLM) agents typically append raw tool outputs to their context.

sents.en: Over multi-step interactions, long and noisy observations incur substantial context overhead and dilute the agent’s attention to task-relevant information.

sents.en: Existing token pruning and summarization methods remain constrained by discrete text representations, limiting the achievable compression ratios.
sents.zh: 现有的 token 剪枝与摘要方法仍受限于离散文本表示，限制了可实现的压缩比率。

paragraphs.en: In this work, we challenge the prevailing assumption that agents must consume tool observations as explicit text tokens. To this end, we propose Coca-Cola, a continuous latent context compression model for LLM agents. Coca-Cola compresses tool observations into latent tokens and embeds them into the input embedding space of the agent. We further introduce Action-Preserving Training , which aligns the agent’s next-action distributions under full and compressed observations. This trains the compression model to learn action-sufficient latent tokens that retain decision-critical information. Experiments with web-search agents on four QA benchmarks and two model families show that Coca-Cola reduces the agent’s token consumption by 70.01%–89.24% and end-to-end runtime by 24.45%–55.97%, while consistently improving task performance. These results suggest that Coca-Cola offers a promising approach for context compression in agents. Our code is available at https://github.com/THU-Agent/Coca-cola .
paragraphs.zh: 在本工作中，我们挑战了一个普遍假设，即智能体必须以显式文本词元的形式消费工具观测。 为此，我们提出了 Coca-Cola，一种面向大语言模型智能体的连续潜在上下文压缩模型。 Coca-Cola 将工具观测压缩为潜在词元，并将其嵌入智能体的输入嵌入空间中。 我们进一步提出了动作保持训练，该方法使智能体在完整观测与压缩观测下的下一动作分布保持一致。 这训练压缩模型学习动作充分的潜在词元，以保留对决策至关重要的信息。 在四个问答基准和两个模型家族上，基于网络搜索智能体的实验表明，Coca-Cola 将智能体的词元消耗降低 70.01%–89.24%，将端到端运行时间降低 24.45%–55.97%，同时持续提升任务性能。 这些结果表明，Coca-Cola 为智能体中的上下文压缩提供了一种有前景的方法。 我们的代码发布于 https://github.com/THU-Agent/Coca-cola 。

paragraphs.en: A natural solution is to compress the agent’s context. Existing methods mainly use token pruning or text summarization. Token pruning uses a model to identify and remove less informative tokens Li et al. (2023) ; Jiang et al. (2023) ; Pan et al. (2024) ; Jiang et al. (2024) . Text summarization uses an auxiliary LLM to condense tool outputs or interaction histories into shorter summaries Wang et al. (2026) ; Xu et al. (2023) . However, such text-level compression has a fundamental flaw: because the compressed result remains a discrete token sequence that must stay semantically coherent, its achievable compression ratio is inherently limited.

paragraphs.en: A closer look at tool–agent interactions raises a fundamental question: must tool outputs be expressed in textual tokens? Since these outputs primarily support an agent’s subsequent reasoning and actions, tool–agent interaction need not rely on explicit textual tokens. This observation motivates us to reconsider how tool information is represented. Compared with discrete text tokens, continuous latent tokens (i.e., high-dimensional vectors in the embedding space) offer a more flexible alternative. These latent tokens can encode rich information compactly under a limited token budget, while their differentiability enables direct optimization for downstream objectives. Recent studies Yu et al. (2026) ; Chen et al. (2026b) have explored latent tokens in reasoning Hao et al. (2024) ; Cheng and Van Durme (2024) ; Xu et al. (2025) ; Deng et al. (2023) ; Anonymous (2026) , agents’ communication Ye et al. (2026) ; Zou et al. (2025) ; Du et al. (2026) ; Jin et al. (2026) , and memory Zhang et al. (2025a) ; Zhang et al. (2026) ; Wang et al. (2024) ; Zhang et al. (2025b) . Together, these studies suggest that models can directly process and exchange information through latent tokens, opening up new possibilities for information transfer between tools and agents.

paragraphs.en: Motivated by this analysis, we propose Coca-Cola ( Co ntext C ompression vi a Co ntinuous La tent Tokens), a latent context compression model for LLM agents. Conditioned on the task instruction and the agent’s current-step reasoning trajectory, Coca-Cola compresses long, noisy tool observations into a few latent tokens that retain information critical to subsequent decisions. These latent tokens are mapped into the agent’s input embedding space, enabling it to use the compressed information for further reasoning and actions.

paragraphs.en: Although latent tokens enable efficient information compression, applying them to compress tool observations for agents introduces two key challenges. The first is to make compressed representations effectively usable by the agent. The second is to preserve decision-critical information under a limited representation budget. To address the first challenge, we design a context-aware encoder with a latent adapter that maps compressed representations into the target agent’s input embedding space. This allows the agent to directly use these latent tokens for subsequent reasoning and actions. For the second challenge, we propose an action-preserving training method. Specifically, we align the agent’s next-action distributions under full and compressed tool observations. This trains the compression model to minimize its impact on the agent’s next-action behavior, thereby preserving action-critical information.

sents.en: Although latent tokens enable efficient information compression, applying them to compress tool observations for agents introduces two key challenges.

sents.zh: 第二个挑战是在有限的表示预算下保留对决策至关重要的信息。

sents.en: This trains the compression model to minimize its impact on the agent’s next-action behavior, thereby preserving action-critical information.

paragraphs.en: We evaluate Coca-Cola across two model configurations and four web-search QA benchmarks. Compared to uncompressed agents, Coca-Cola reduces total token consumption by 70.01%–89.24% and end-to-end runtime by 24.45%–55.97%, demonstrating substantial efficiency gains. Despite aggressive compression, Coca-Cola consistently outperforms the uncompressed agent in both EM and F1, and achieves the best EM and F1 among all methods in six of the eight model–dataset settings.

paragraphs.en: In recent years, continuous latent tokens have been explored for reasoning, communication, and memory in large language agents. For latent reasoning, Coconut ( Hao et al., 2024 ) , CCoT ( Cheng and Van Durme, 2024 ) , and SoftCoT ( Xu et al., 2025 ) explore reasoning in continuous latent spaces, reducing reliance on explicit natural-language reasoning processes. For agent communication, KVComm ( Ye et al., 2026 ) and LatentMAS ( Zou et al., 2025 ) investigate information exchange between agents through hidden states or KV caches. For memory, MemGen ( Zhang et al., 2025a ) and NextMem ( Zhang et al., 2026 ) explore storing and utilizing historical information through continuous latent tokens. These studies demonstrate that latent tokens can support both internal information processing and inter-model communication, offering new possibilities beyond traditional text-based interactions.
paragraphs.zh: 近年来，连续潜在token在大语言智能体的推理、通信与记忆方面得到了探索。 在潜在推理方面，Coconut（Hao et al., 2024）、CCoT（Cheng and Van Durme, 2024）和SoftCoT（Xu et al., 2025）探索在连续潜在空间中进行推理，减少了对显式自然语言推理过程的依赖。 在智能体通信方面，KVComm（Ye et al., 2026）和LatentMAS（Zou et al., 2025）研究通过隐藏状态或KV缓存实现智能体之间的信息交换。 在记忆方面，MemGen（Zhang et al., 2025a）和NextMem（Zhang et al., 2026）探索通过连续潜在token来存储和利用历史信息。 这些研究表明，潜在token既能支持内部信息处理，也能支持模型间通信，为超越传统基于文本的交互提供了新的可能。

paragraphs.en: As shown in Figure 2 , we propose Coca-Cola, a continuous latent context compression model for LLM agents. Unlike traditional text-based compression methods, Coca-Cola compresses lengthy tool observations into a small number of latent tokens to reduce the context overhead of tool interactions. We first theoretically analyze the information capacity of latent tokens, providing theoretical motivation for compressing tool observations into continuous vectors (Section 3.2 ).
paragraphs.zh: 如图2所示，我们提出了Coca-Cola，一种用于LLM智能体的连续潜在上下文压缩模型。 与传统的基于文本的压缩方法不同，Coca-Cola将冗长的工具观测压缩为少量潜在标记，以减少工具交互带来的上下文开销。 我们首先从理论上分析潜在标记的信息容量，为将工具观测压缩为连续向量提供了理论依据（见3.2节）。

paragraphs.en: Specifically, after each tool call, Coca-Cola takes the task instruction, the agent’s current-step reasoning trajectory, and the tool observation as input. A lightweight encoder processes these inputs, while a latent adapter maps the resulting latent tokens into the target agent’s input embedding space (Section 3.3 ). To preserve decision-critical information under a limited representation budget, we further introduce Action-Preserving Training , which trains the compressor by aligning the agent’s next-action distributions under full and compressed observations(Section 3.4 ). During inference, the trained compressor replaces raw tool observations with latent tokens after each tool call, allowing the agent to perform multi-step interactions with a more compact context (Section 3.5 ).
paragraphs.zh: 具体而言，在每次工具调用之后，Coca-Cola 以任务指令、智能体当前步骤的推理轨迹以及工具观测作为输入。 一个轻量级编码器处理这些输入，同时一个潜在适配器将生成的潜在 token 映射到目标智能体的输入嵌入空间（第 3.3 节）。 为了在有限的表示预算下保留对决策至关重要的信息，我们进一步提出动作保持训练，通过在全量观测和压缩观测下对齐智能体的下一步动作分布来训练压缩器（第 3.4 节）。 在推理阶段，训练好的压缩器在每次工具调用后用潜在 token 替代原始工具观测，使智能体能够以更紧凑的上下文执行多步交互（第 3.5 节）。

paragraphs.en: Coca-Cola substantially reduces tool-context overhead. Compared with the Vanilla Model, which directly incorporates full tool observations into the agent’s context, Coca-Cola consistently reduces both input and output token consumption across all evaluated datasets. For instance, on NQ with the Qwen models, the average number of input tokens decreases from 14,362.12 to 1,766.53, representing an 87.70% reduction. Similarly, on 2Wiki with the GLM models, input token consumption drops from 31,693.47 to 3,003.38, corresponding to a 90.52% reduction. These results demonstrate that replacing noisy tool observations with compact latent tokens effectively mitigates context growth while reducing subsequent generation overhead.

paragraphs.en: Coca-Cola achieves high compression rates across all settings. paragraphs.en: High compression rates do not compromise task performance, but can even lead to improvements. Compared with the Vanilla Model, Coca-Cola consistently achieves higher EM and F1 across all evaluated settings. On TriviaQA with Qwen, Coca-Cola improves F1 from 62.87% to 67.07% while achieving an 83.68% compression rate. Similarly, on 2Wiki with GLM, F1 increases from 31.29% to 36.20% at an 89.24% compression rate. paragraphs.en: Coca-Cola outperforms existing compression methods in most settings. paragraphs.en: In this paper, we introduce Coca-Cola, a continuous latent context compression model for compacting noisy tool observations in LLM agents. Unlike conventional token pruning and summarization methods, Coca-Cola encodes tool outputs into a small number of task-conditioned latent tokens that are directly injected into the agent. Through our action-preserving training, we learn a compression model that preserves decision-critical information rather than reconstructing the original observations. Experiments on web-search tasks demonstrate that Coca-Cola substantially reduces context overhead while consistently improving task performance.
paragraphs.zh: 在本文中，我们提出 Coca-Cola，这是一种连续潜在上下文压缩模型，用于压缩大语言模型智能体中含噪的工具观测。 与传统的 token 剪枝和摘要方法不同，Coca-Cola 将工具输出编码为少量任务条件化的潜在 token，并直接注入智能体。 通过我们提出的动作保持训练，我们学习到一个压缩模型，它保留对决策至关重要的信息，而不是重构原始观测。 在网页搜索任务上的实验表明，Coca-Cola 在显著降低上下文开销的同时，能够持续提升任务性能。

sents.zh: 通过我们提出的动作保持训练，我们学习到一个压缩模型，它保留对决策至关重要的信息，而不是重构原始观测。

sents.en: Experiments on web-search tasks demonstrate that Coca-Cola substantially reduces context overhead while consistently improving task performance.
sents.zh: 在网页搜索任务上的实验表明，Coca-Cola 在显著降低上下文开销的同时，能够持续提升任务性能。

paragraphs.en: More fundamentally, we challenge a prevailing assumption in LLM agents: interaction between tools and agents need not rely on explicit text tokens. Instead, tools only need to convey information sufficient for subsequent decisions through compact, latent tokens. This perspective opens a promising direction for building more efficient and scalable long-horizon agents.
paragraphs.zh: 更根本地，我们挑战了大语言模型智能体中一个普遍假设：工具与智能体之间的交互不必依赖显式的文本词元。 相反，工具只需通过紧凑的潜在词元传递足以支持后续决策的信息。 这一视角为构建更高效、更可扩展的长程智能体开辟了一个有前景的方向。

paragraphs.en: We construct the compression dataset from 4,188 distinct tasks, containing 4,363 tool observation–action pairs. We reserve 10% of the pairs for validation, yielding 3,927 training pairs and 436 validation pairs.
paragraphs.zh: 我们从4,188个不同的任务构建压缩数据集，包含4,363个工具观测–动作对。 我们保留10%的数据对用于验证，得到3,927个训练数据对和436个验证数据对。

paragraphs.en: The target agent remains frozen throughout training. We update only the LoRA parameters of the context-aware model and the parameters of the latent adapter. The LoRA rank, scaling factor, and dropout rate are set to 16, 32, and 0.05, respectively.
paragraphs.zh: 目标智能体在整个训练过程中保持冻结。 我们仅更新上下文感知模型的 LoRA 参数以及潜在适配器的参数。 LoRA 的秩、缩放因子和丢弃率分别设置为 16、32 和 0.05。

sents.zh: 目标智能体在整个训练过程中保持冻结。

sents.zh: 我们仅更新上下文感知模型的 LoRA 参数以及潜在适配器的参数。

sents.en: The LoRA rank, scaling factor, and dropout rate are set to 16, 32, and 0.05, respectively.

paragraphs.en: We use paged 8-bit AdamW as the optimizer, with initial learning rates of 1.5 × 10 − 4 1.5\times 10^{-4} for both the LoRA parameters and the latent adapter. The learning rate decays linearly to 5 × 10 − 5 5\times 10^{-5} . The weight decay is set to 0. The loss weights λ KL \lambda_{\mathrm{KL}} and λ CE \lambda_{\mathrm{CE}} are set to 0.3 and 1.0, respectively. The KL loss weight is warmed up over the first 20% of training steps.
paragraphs.zh: 我们使用分页 8 位 AdamW 作为优化器，LoRA 参数与潜在适配器的初始学习率均为 1.5 × 10 − 4 1.5\times 10^{-4}。 学习率线性衰减至 5 × 10 − 5 5\times 10^{-5}。 权重衰减设置为 0。 损失权重 λ KL \lambda_{\mathrm{KL}} 和 λ CE \lambda_{\mathrm{CE}} 分别设置为 0.3 和 1.0。 KL 损失权重在训练的前 20% 步数内进行预热。

paragraphs.en: During inference, each tool observation is compressed into 128 continuous latent tokens and directly injected into the target agent’s input embedding sequence.
paragraphs.zh: 在推理过程中，每个工具观测都被压缩为 128 个连续的潜在标记，并直接注入目标智能体的输入嵌入序列中。

paragraphs.en: For web search, we retrieve up to 5 results per tool call and allow a maximum of 5 tool calls per task.
paragraphs.zh: 对于网页搜索，我们每次工具调用最多检索 5 条结果，并且每个任务最多允许 5 次工具调用。

paragraphs.en: All experiments are conducted on 4 NVIDIA A100-SXM4 GPUs, each with 80 GB of memory.
paragraphs.zh: 所有实验均在 4 块 NVIDIA A100-SXM4 GPU 上进行，每块 GPU 拥有 80 GB 显存。

paragraphs.en: For Coca-Cola, the frozen target agent is distributed across 3 GPUs, while the context-aware encoder and the latent adapter are placed on the remaining GPU.
paragraphs.zh: 对于可口可乐（Coca-Cola），冻结的目标智能体分布在 3 个 GPU 上，而上下文感知编码器和潜在适配器则放置在剩余的 GPU 上。

paragraphs.en: All inference results, including the runtimes reported in Tables 1 and 2 , are obtained with the target agent running on a single GPU in all settings. Where an additional GPU is used, it hosts only the compression model.
paragraphs.zh: 所有推理结果（包括表1和表2中报告的运行时间）均在所有设置下由目标智能体在单张GPU上运行获得。 在使用额外GPU的情况下，该GPU仅用于承载压缩模型。

paragraphs.en: Figure 5 presents the prompt used to guide the agent in web-search-based question answering. The prompt specifies the search tool interface, the maximum number of search attempts, and the required final-answer format. It also provides an example of multi-step search to illustrate how the agent can iteratively retrieve information and reason over search results.
paragraphs.zh: 图 5 展示了用于指导智能体进行基于网络搜索问答的提示词。 该提示词规定了搜索工具接口、最大搜索次数以及最终答案的格式要求。 它还提供了一个多步搜索的示例，以说明智能体如何迭代地检索信息并对搜索结果进行推理。
